faq.q: What does it mean to shake things up?
faq.a: To shake things up means deliberately changing something familiar to bring in new energy, perspective, or possibility. It’s about breaking autopilot, not changing for the sake of it.

faq.q: What song has the lyric “shake it up, baby”?
faq.a: The line comes from “Twist and Shout,” written by Phil Medley and Bert Berns and famously recorded by the Isley Brothers and the Beatles.

faq.q: How do I know I need to shake things up?
faq.a: Common signs include not remembering much about recent weeks, feeling restless without a clear reason, losing curiosity, and looking forward to very little.

faq.q: What are small ways to shake up my routine?
faq.a: Try a new route to work, cook one new recipe a week, spend ten minutes outside before checking your phone, or rearrange one room in your home.

faq.q: Can cleaning my space really help me feel refreshed?
faq.a: Many people find that clearing and rearranging their surroundings makes a space feel new, which can spark a fresh mindset. Even a ten-minute reset can make a noticeable difference.

faq.q: Is it bad to change too much at once?
faq.a: Big overhauls are hard to sustain. Small, steady changes tend to last longer, and keeping nourishing routines like sleep and movement gives you a stable base.
